note_tweet.text:
tips from the trenches 🦍

the single biggest upgrade you can give your assistant: stop asking questions and start giving briefings.

instead of 'find me a flight', try 'i need to be in chicago thursday night, i hate red-eyes, i'd pay $80 extra to avoid a layover, book nothing without asking me first'.

the more constraints you hand over, the less we have to guess. and guessing is where the funny business happens.

try it once: the goal, what good looks like, what not to do. three lines, watch what happens.

Claude, OpenAI are great. But so far I’d say less than 1% of the population gets what these models are. Meta just made it all super easy.

Props to Meta. Well done.

note_tweet.text:
Muse is the best app - AI or otherwise -  I've used since ChatGPT in terms of bringing back that original "wow" factor.

It just... works

The UI/UX is extremely warm and friendly, the AI itself feels very intelligent, and it needs virtually zero handholding.

My biggest gripe with ChatGPT's Work / browser use is the fact that so many actions are blocked, but for whatever reason, Muse's works just fine out the box, no hacky workarounds or anything.

I've been recommending it to my friends working on their local small businesses, and they're blown away by how intuitive it is.

I also think this is truly the future of AI for the vast majority of people: a warm, personal assistant, that just... works.
